skill.name: convex-crons
skill.description: Create reliable recurring jobs for Convex applications using internal functions, sensible intervals, and idempotent handlers.
skill.summary: Guide Convex cron design with safe schedules and repeatable handlers.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable code or static findings. Its instructions focus on internal Convex functions, idempotent handlers, sensible intervals, and dashboard verification.

content.value_statement: Recurring jobs can fail, duplicate work, or expose public functions when schedules and handlers are poorly designed. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create safe Convex schedules with internal, idempotent, small handlers.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of the Convex cron configuration in convex/crons.ts.
Directs schedules to internal functions instead of public API functions.
Recommends intervals suited to the requested recurring task.
Promotes idempotent handlers that remain safe when repeated.
Keeps each scheduled run small and focused.
Includes dashboard verification of the resulting schedule.
limitations: Requires a Convex application with an existing target function.
Does not determine business-specific schedules without clear timing requirements.
Does not provide runtime monitoring, alerting, or failure recovery.
Covers recurring cron jobs, not event-driven subscriptions or one-time scheduled functions.

use_cases.title: Schedule Routine Maintenance
use_cases.description: Create recurring cleanup or archival jobs with small, repeatable handlers.

use_cases.title: Automate Product Operations
use_cases.description: Plan periodic reminders, status updates, or summary generation without exposing public functions.

use_cases.title: Review Cron Reliability
use_cases.description: Check existing schedules for unsafe targets, tight polling, large runs, and non-idempotent behavior.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads reviewing Convex backend changes

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Schedule
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a Convex cron job that runs [internal function] every [interval]. Keep the handler small and idempotent, then explain dashboard verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when adding one straightforward recurring task.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Suitable Interval
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Convex schedule for [task and business requirement]. Recommend a sensible interval and explain why subscription-based updates are or are not better.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the correct execution frequency is unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Cron Jobs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Convex cron configuration and handlers. Identify public function targets, tight polling, oversized runs, and non-idempotent operations. Propose focused corrections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when improving an existing cron implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reliable Recurring Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design recurring Convex jobs for [workflow]. Define internal targets, intervals, idempotency strategy, bounded batch sizes, retry behavior, and dashboard verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for multiple related jobs with reliability requirements.

output_examples.input: Schedule a daily cleanup of expired sessions.
output: Use one daily schedule targeting an internal cleanup function.
Delete expired sessions in bounded batches and make repeated execution harmless.
Confirm the job and next run time in the Convex dashboard.

output_examples.input: Review a job that checks for updates every minute.
output_examples.output: The interval may be unnecessary for data that subscriptions can push. Replace polling with reactive updates, or document the need for minute-level checks.

output: Schedule an internal summary function once each week.
Record completed periods so retries do not create duplicate summaries.
Process accounts in small batches to keep each run bounded.

best_practices: Target internal functions so scheduled operations are not exposed through the public API.
Design every handler to produce the same safe result when repeated.
Use moderate intervals and bounded work, then verify schedules in the dashboard.
anti_patterns: Do not schedule public API functions for internal recurring work.
Do not use tight polling when subscriptions can deliver updates.
Do not place large, non-idempotent workloads in a single cron run.

faq.question: What file contains Convex cron schedules?
faq.answer: Define recurring jobs in convex/crons.ts using the Convex cron job configuration.

faq.question: Should a cron target a public API function?
faq.answer: No. Target an internal function to keep scheduled operations private.

faq.question: Why must handlers be idempotent?
faq.answer: Retries or repeated runs can occur. Idempotency prevents duplicate or inconsistent effects.

faq.question: How should I choose an interval?
faq.answer: Match the interval to the business requirement and avoid frequent polling when subscriptions can push changes.

faq.question: How much work should one run perform?
faq.answer: Keep each run small and bounded. Divide larger workloads into controlled batches.

faq.question: How do I confirm the schedule is active?
faq.answer: Check the Convex dashboard schedule after deployment and verify the expected job and interval.
